definitions.gloss: complete recovery; full healing (from injury or illness)
definitions.explanation: Full healing of an injury or illness to the point of complete cure. Most often stated as a length of time, as in {全治|ぜんち}{二週間|にしゅうかん} ("two weeks to fully heal"). Takes する.

examples.japanese: {全治|ぜんち}{一|いっ}ヶ{月|げつ}のけがだ。
examples.english: It's an injury that will take a month to fully heal.

examples.japanese: {骨折|こっせつ}したが、{全治|ぜんち}までは{三|さん}ヶ{月|げつ}かかるそうだ。
examples.english: I broke a bone, and apparently it will take three months to heal completely.

examples.japanese: {選手|せんしゅ}は{全治|ぜんち}{二週間|にしゅうかん}の{捻挫|ねんざ}で、{次|つぎ}の{試合|しあい}は{欠場|けつじょう}する。
examples.english: The player has a sprain needing two weeks to heal and will sit out the next game.

notes:
Composed of {全|ぜん} (complete) + {治|ち} (cure). Typically paired with a time estimate to express how long full recovery will take.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全治|ぜんち}{二週間|にしゅうかん}: two weeks to fully recover
- {全治|ぜんち}する: to heal completely
- {全治|ぜんち}までかかる: to take (a period) until full recovery

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {完治|かんじ}: complete cure — emphasizes the cured state itself; {全治|ぜんち} is more often used with a time estimate
- {治療|ちりょう}: treatment — the process of treating, not the recovery

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: 全治していませんでした
